newsitem.title: TANZANIA: U.N. agency says not responsible for Zaire troops.
newsitem.headline: U.N. agency says not responsible for Zaire troops.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday it was not responsible for Zairean soldiers who fled fighting in eastern Zaire to Tanzania and were threatened with deportation for unruly behaviour.
Some 220 Zairean soldiers who fled across Lake Tanganyika to the Tanzanian port of Kigoma are detained at a government holding centre. Tanzanian officials say they are violent and unruly.
"They came armed and we don't encourage arms in the country," said an official of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). "We're trying as much as possible not to touch them".
He said none of the soldiers had requested refugee status.

The state-owned Daily News on Monday quoted the Kigoma regional commissioner as saying the authorities would ask the government, UNHCR and International Committee of the Red Cross to take the soldiers elsewhere.
"These people are a problem. They are rude, violent and totally uncooperative," said Kigoma Commissioner Yusuf Mkamba.
Home Affairs (Interior) Minister Ali Mohamed said he supported moves to deport the troublesome Zairean soldiers.
UNHCR said 241,760 Burundian and Zairean refugees were registered in Kigoma region. Zairean refugees continue to cross Lake Tanganyika at an average of more than 1,000 every day.
